title: Cycle orthogonality splits extensions of acyclic complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $X,Y$ be integer cochain complexes, meaning $d^{n+1}d^n=0$, and put $Z^nX=\ker d_X^n$ and $Z^nY=\ker d_Y^n$. Assume both complexes are acyclic, that is $\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}=\ker d^n$ in every degree. Suppose $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Z^iX,Z^jY)=0$ for every $i,j\in\mathbf Z$, where this means every short exact extension of $Z^iX$ by $Z^jY$ splits. Then every short exact sequence $0\to Y\to E\xrightarrow{p}X\to0$ in the category of cochain complexes admits a cochain map $s:X\to E$ with $ps=1_X$.

source.place: Agent-formulated tool for proof paragraph 2: Splitting a complex extension by choosing cycle sections and adjusting term sections; WANTED: Gillespie (2004), Lemma 3.10. Agent-formulated general extension lemma; no Stacks tag states the whole assertion.

proof.text: Write $j_X^n:Z^nX\to X^n$ and $q_X^n:X^n\to Z^{n+1}X$ with $d_X^n=j_X^{n+1}q_X^n$, and similarly $j_Y^n,q_Y^n$. Acyclicity and the definitions of image and kernel give short exact rows $0\to Z^nX\xrightarrow{j_X^n}X^n\xrightarrow{q_X^n}Z^{n+1}X\to0$, and the analogous rows for $Y$. Each $q_X^n$ is a cokernel of $j_X^n$ by the cited cokernel statement. The given extension $0\to Y\xrightarrow{\iota}E\xrightarrow{p}X\to0$ is degreewise short exact: kernels of cochain maps are the termwise kernels, with differentials induced by the kernel universal property, and cokernels are constructed dually, so exactness is computed in each degree. Thus $\iota^n$ is a kernel of $p^n$. All subsequent factorizations use these kernel and cokernel universal properties.

source.place: Tags 0109 (definition-abelian-category), 010E (definition-exact); agent application of kernel/cokernel universal properties to complexes and cycle rows.

proof.text: Use $U\perp_1 V$ in the precise splitting sense of [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus]. Put $\mathcal S=\{Z^iX:i\in\mathbf Z\}$. Every $Z^jY$ lies in $\mathcal S^{\perp_1}$ by hypothesis. Extension closure of this right orthogonal, applied to the $Y$ cycle row, gives $Y^j\in\mathcal S^{\perp_1}$, hence $Z^iX\perp_1Y^j$ for all $i,j$. Now put $\mathcal T=\{Y^j:j\in\mathbf Z\}$. Every $Z^iX$ lies in ${}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$, and extension closure of this left orthogonal, applied to the $X$ cycle row, gives $X^i\perp_1Y^j$ for all $i,j$. Only the two extension-closure clauses of the cited statement are used; no complete cotorsion pair or higher Ext hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Derived coefficient adjunction paragraph; agent argument reducing term extensions to the cycle orthogonality hypothesis using the existing extension calculus.

proof.text: For each $n$ choose a section $t^n:X^n\to E^n$ of $p^n$, possible by $X^n\perp_1Y^n$ from step 2. The map $d_E^nt^n-t^{n+1}d_X^n$ is killed by $p^{n+1}$, since $p$ is a cochain map and $p^nt^n=1$. It therefore factors uniquely as $\iota^{n+1}a^n$ for $a^n:X^n\to Y^{n+1}$. Expanding the square of the differential gives $\iota^{n+2}(d_Y^{n+1}a^n+a^{n+1}d_X^n)=0$, hence $d_Y^{n+1}a^n+a^{n+1}d_X^n=0$ by monicity. Explicitly the expansion is $d_E^{n+1}(d_E^nt^n-t^{n+1}d_X^n)+(d_E^{n+1}t^{n+1}-t^{n+2}d_X^{n+1})d_X^n=0$.

source.place: Derived coefficient adjunction paragraph; agent construction of the differential defect of a graded section. Compare the explicit cocycle formula in Mathlib Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory/DegreewiseSplit.lean:43-64.

proof.text: The cocycle identity in step 3 implies $d_Y^{n+1}a^nj_X^n=0$. Factor through the kernel to obtain $f^n:Z^nX\to Z^{n+1}Y$ with $j_Y^{n+1}f^n=a^nj_X^n$. Apply the diagonal-filler clause of [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus] to the monomorphism $0\to Z^nX$ and epimorphism $q_Y^n:Y^n\to Z^{n+1}Y$, with bottom map $f^n$ and zero top map. Its cokernel is $Z^nX$ and its kernel is $Z^nY$, which are orthogonal by the original hypothesis. We obtain $c^n:Z^nX\to Y^n$ with $q_Y^nc^n=f^n$. This is a lift for each integer $n$, independently of the other degrees.

source.place: Derived coefficient adjunction paragraph; first pass, lift the restriction of the defect to the cycles. The supporting filler is the existing splitting-orthogonality calculus, not an injectivity assumption.

proof.text: Extend $c^n$ to a map $b^n:X^n\to Y^n$ using the same diagonal-filler clause, now for $j_X^n:Z^nX\to X^n$ and $Y^n\to0$, with top map $c^n$ and zero bottom map. The monomorphism has cokernel $Z^{n+1}X$ by step 1, the epimorphism has kernel $Y^n$, and $Z^{n+1}X\perp_1Y^n$ was proved in step 2. Thus $b^nj_X^n=c^n$. Define $r^n=a^n-d_Y^nb^n+b^{n+1}d_X^n$. Then $r^nj_X^n=a^nj_X^n-j_Y^{n+1}q_Y^nc^n=0$.

source.place: Derived coefficient adjunction paragraph; first pass, extend the chosen cycle lifts over each term, using precisely the cycle-to-term orthogonality from step 2.

proof.text: The residual satisfies $d_Y^{n+1}r^n+r^{n+1}d_X^n=0$: substitute its definition, use the identity for $a$, and cancel the two mixed terms; the remaining two terms vanish by $d_Y^2=d_X^2=0$. Since $r^{n+1}j_X^{n+1}=0$ and $d_X^n=j_X^{n+1}q_X^n$, we have $r^{n+1}d_X^n=0$, hence $d_Y^{n+1}r^n=0$. By the cokernel property of $q_X^n$, the equality $r^nj_X^n=0$ gives $r^n=v^nq_X^n$ for $v^n:Z^{n+1}X\to Y^{n+1}$. Epic cancellation of $q_X^n$ gives $d_Y^{n+1}v^n=0$. Factoring through its kernel produces $w^n:Z^{n+1}X\to Z^{n+1}Y$ with $r^n=j_Y^{n+1}w^nq_X^n$.

source.place: Derived coefficient adjunction paragraph; agent residual calculation, using the cokernel factorization in homology.tex, Tag 010E, and the kernel universal property.

proof.text: Apply the diagonal-filler clause once more, to $0\to Z^{n+1}X$ and $q_Y^n:Y^n\to Z^{n+1}Y$, with bottom map $w^n$. Its orthogonality hypothesis is exactly $Z^{n+1}X\perp_1Z^nY$, which is part of the original hypothesis. Choose $u^n:Z^{n+1}X\to Y^n$ with $q_Y^nu^n=w^n$, and set $k^n=u^nq_X^n$. Then $k^{n+1}d_X^n=0$, since $q_X^{n+1}j_X^{n+1}=0$, and $d_Y^nk^n=j_Y^{n+1}q_Y^nu^nq_X^n=r^n$. Therefore, with $h^n=b^n+k^n$, the definition of $r$ gives $d_Y^nh^n-h^{n+1}d_X^n=a^n$. This second pass removes the residual without changing the first-pass restrictions on cycles.

source.place: Derived coefficient adjunction paragraph; second pass, lift the residual cycle-valued maps. All choices are independent by degree, so no boundedness or induction from a first degree is required.

proof.text: Define $s^n=t^n-\iota^nh^n$. Then $p^ns^n=1_{X^n}$ because $p^n\iota^n=0$. As $\iota$ is a cochain map, $d_E^ns^n-s^{n+1}d_X^n=\iota^{n+1}(a^n-d_Y^nh^n+h^{n+1}d_X^n)=0$ by step 7. Thus the maps $s^n$ form the required cochain section $s:X\to E$, and $ps=1_X$.
